title: The verifier runs migrations on a disposable PostgreSQL and always tears it down
description:
SPIDR child 2 of task-8f86e10504c74e248ccfa6f427b41a15 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 task-463f195efd2f4fd2886790029a474194 for the `db:migrate` script it detects.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the verifier's DATABASE leg. When a workspace declares `db:migrate`, start a disposable PostgreSQL container on a random port, export DATABASE_URL to the recipe, run the migrations, THEN the tests, then tear the container down ON EVERY EXIT PATH. No deploy, no UI.

THE CONTAINER TEARDOWN IS THE SUBJECT, exactly as the preview runner's process cleanup was. A leaked container holds its port and its disk; the next verification then fails to bind and the failure appears far from its cause. The parent's DoD 1 requires the container gone after ACCEPT, after REJECT, AND after a forced kill - assert by asking DOCKER whether the container exists, never by an internal flag.

DOCKER ABSENT REFUSES, NEVER SKIPS. `MIGRATION_DB_UNAVAILABLE` with its layer, recorded as a refusal with a reason - the parent is explicit that the verifier NEVER SILENTLY SKIPS. A silent skip would let a node pass verification on a machine without docker while its migrations were never run, which is the worst outcome available here: a green node whose schema change was never executed.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb: the verifier runs the node's `test` recipe in the workspace with NO database (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-verifier.ts, 230 lines; verifier-process-runner.ts, 395 lines). verifier-process-runner already has exactly the machinery this row needs and must reuse: injectable `spawn`, `timeoutMs`, `killGraceMs` and `killProcessGroup` (options at :49-55), a process-GROUP SIGKILL at :187-189, and timer cleanup on every exit path (:110-114). Read it before writing a container lifecycle - the shape of 'always clean up' is already solved there for processes.

ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING: migrations run BEFORE the tests. A test suite that runs against an unmigrated schema fails for a reason that looks like a product bug.
definitionOfDone: With a workspace declaring `db:migrate`, the verifier starts a disposable PostgreSQL on a RANDOM port, and the test proves DATABASE_URL REACHED THE RECIPE - assert from the recipe's own output or environment, not from the daemon's intent.

MIGRATIONS RAN BEFORE THE TESTS: assert the ordering observably (the migrated table exists at the moment the test recipe starts, or the recipe's output shows the migration first). A suite running against an unmigrated schema fails looking like a product bug.

THE CONTAINER IS GONE after ACCEPT, after REJECT, and after a FORCED KILL - three arms, each asserted by asking DOCKER whether the container exists, never by an internal flag. A leaked container holds its port and the NEXT verification fails to bind, far from the cause.

DOCKER ABSENT REFUSES MIGRATION_DB_UNAVAILABLE with its layer and is RECORDED AS A REFUSAL WITH A REASON - never a silent skip and never a pass. Assert the node does NOT reach ACCEPTED on that path: a green node whose migrations never ran is the worst outcome this row can produce.
MIGRATION_FAILED carries THE FAILING FILE (code + layer asserted): a migration failure that does not name which migration failed sends a seat to read all of them.

The random port genuinely avoids collision: two disposable databases can exist concurrently without one taking the other's port - assert with two simultaneous verifications, since parallel node staffing (task-92d84d38) makes concurrent verification the normal case, not an edge case.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: TEARDOWN ON EVERY EXIT PATH, asserted against DOCKER rather than a flag. A flag proves the code believed it cleaned up.
NEVER SILENTLY SKIP THE DATABASE LEG. Docker absent is a refusal with a code; a skip would let a node pass verification with its migrations unrun.

REUSE verifier-process-runner.ts's lifecycle discipline (injectable spawn/timeout/killGrace, process-group kill, cleanup on every path). A second independently-written lifecycle is how one of them leaks.
MIGRATIONS BEFORE TESTS, always, and provably.
CONCURRENT VERIFICATIONS ARE NORMAL now that nodes staff in parallel - the port strategy must survive two at once.

implementationPlan.description: THE DISPOSABLE DATABASE, IN ITS OWN MODULE. NEW FILE `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/verifier-database.ts` plus its `.js` bridge (the orchestrator directory pairs every module with one; a missing bridge kills the daemon at boot with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND). It owns: detect, start, migrate, tear down. LET DOCKER CHOOSE THE PORT - THIS IS THE ONE DESIGN DECISION IN THE ROW AND THE OBVIOUS APPROACH IS RACY. Picking a free port in Node and passing `-p <chosen>:5432` has a TOCTOU window: the port is free when you look and taken when docker binds, and DoD-6 makes concurrent verifications the normal case, so that race is not hypothetical. Publish with `-p 0:5432` and read the assigned port back with `docker port <container> 5432` - docker binds first and tells you after, so there is no window. State that choice in the module docblock so the next reader does not 'simplify' it back into a race. NAME THE CONTAINER UNIQUELY per verification (the node ref plus a random suffix) so two concurrent runs cannot collide on a name either, and so the teardown arms can ask docker about a specific container rather than about 'the' container. WAIT FOR READY, DO NOT SLEEP: postgres accepts TCP before it accepts queries. Poll `pg_isready` (or an equivalent the image ships) until it answers or a bounded budget expires, and refuse on expiry rather than proceeding to a migration that will fail confusingly. ONE TEARDOWN FUNCTION, CALLED ON EVERY PATH, mirroring the runner's `cleanup()` shape - and it must be safe to call twice, because the forced-kill arm will. Spawn `docker` as a bare executable under `shell: false` with an ARGV ARRAY - never a shell string, never a chain. Take `spawn` injectable, exactly as the process runner does, so the tests in step 4 can drive every branch without a real daemon.
